question: Why does identifying the self with the body prevent liberation even at death?
premises: In the mind, self-identity extends only up to the existence of the body.
If that identity remains, human ignorance is not removed.
Without the removal of human ignorance, liberation does not occur even when the body ends.
inference: Therefore, mere bodily death cannot bring liberation as long as the self is identified with the body.
uncertainties: The exact scope of pauruṣa-ajñāna (human or personal ignorance) is compressed in the compound.
plain_english: Because the mind takes the self to last only as long as the body exists, there would be no liberation even at the end of the body, since human ignorance would still not have been removed.
